ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Provisional Ball
group: General Play – Ball Lost or Out of Bounds
imagePrompt: A polished, modern semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) of a golfer on the 8th hole fairway, next to a white out of bounds fence. The golfer is preparing to drop a ball just inside the fence line, where their original ball crossed out of bounds. The original ball can be seen lying out of play on the other side of the fence. The image should clearly show the fence with white stakes and the boundary between the golf course and out of bounds area. imageAlt: A golfer on the fairway beside an out of bounds fence, preparing to drop a ball where the original ball crossed out of bounds. The original ball is visible out of play beyond the white stakes.

sceneSpec.setting: A fairway on the 8th hole, beside a white out of bounds fence running along one edge of the hole.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer dressed in typical golf attire, preparing to drop a ball close to the out of bounds fence.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball is in the grass just inside the boundary, very near to but not over the white out of bounds line.

sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Clarifying the correct procedure when a ball is out of bounds.
mustShow: Player holding or dropping a golf ball near the boundary
Original ball visible out of play beyond the fence (e.g., in rough or outside course boundary)

questions.title: What To Do When Your Ball Goes Out of Bounds
questions.question: On the 8th hole, your ball goes over the fence and out of bounds. You went to where it crossed and dropped a new ball there, adding one penalty shot. Is this the right thing to do?

choices.text: Yes, that is the right way.
Yes, but only if the golf course has a special rule.
No, this is not allowed by the normal rules.
You have to play a provisional ball.

questions.explanation: If your ball goes out of bounds, the rules say you must take a one-shot penalty and play a new ball from the same spot where you hit the last shot. You are not allowed to just drop a ball where it went out, unless there is a special rule for your course.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When your ball goes over fences or beyond white stakes, it’s outside the golf course.
A second ball you hit just in case your first ball might be lost or out of bounds.
This means you take a penalty shot and hit again from where you last played.

questions.teachingTip: Remind golfers to watch for white stakes or fences that mark out of bounds. Show them where to play from if their ball goes out.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids think you can always just drop a ball where it went out.
Some may not know what a provisional ball is.

questions.title: Procedure When a Ball is Out of Bounds
questions.question: Your ball crosses an out of bounds fence on the 8th hole. You find where it crossed and drop a ball there under one penalty stroke. What is the ruling?

choices.text: Correct only if a Local Rule is in place.
Incorrect under the Rules of Golf.
You must play a provisional ball.

questions.explanation: Under the standard Rules of Golf, if a ball is out of bounds, the player must take stroke and distance relief by playing another ball from where the previous stroke was made, under penalty of one stroke. Dropping a ball at the point it crossed the boundary is not allowed unless a Local Rule specifically permits it.
